svg.text: MCP vs Traditional APIs: Why AI Agents Need a New Integration Standard
• N x M custom glue for every app/service
• Static tool schemas baked into prompts
• No shared resources, prompts, or state
• Write server once, use in any MCP client
• Open standard; donated to Linux Foundation
• Sampling - server can ask the client's LLM to generate
• Roots - client tells server which resources are in scope
• Elicitation - server can ask user for input mid-call
• Transports: stdio for local, HTTP/SSE for remote
REST schemas are static payload that the developer
must maintain per client. MCP schemas are discovered
live at connection time, travel separately from the
prompt, and update automatically when the server
changes. Tool catalogs are cacheable across runs.
The N x M Integration Problem
Before: N apps x M services
Each app ships its own wrapper
• Tools are private to one application
• Tight coupling with app business logic
• Fastest path to ship a prototype
• Same tool needed across multiple clients
MCP does not replace function calling - it sits above it
